comments.body:
🚨 **BLOCKING: red CI gate — `unnecessary_brace_in_string_interps`**

The "Static gates" CI job fails on this PR (`dart analyze --fatal-infos --fatal-warnings`, exit 1):

```
info - test/cli/self_manage_test.dart:1845:51 - Unnecessary braces in a string interpolation. Try removing the braces. - unnecessary_brace_in_string_interps
```

Reproduced locally with the same single issue. The line:

```dart
expect(request.headers['range'], 'bytes=${chunk}-');
```

`chunk` is a simple identifier and the next character (`-`) cannot continue an identifier, so the braces are unnecessary:

```dart
expect(request.headers['range'], 'bytes=$chunk-');
```

(For completeness: the `##[error]size budget regression …` lines earlier in the same CI log are expected fixtures printed by `scripts/test_size_manifest.py`'s own test suite — that step passes. The only real gate failure is this lint.)

comments.author: unknown
comments.body:
💡 **SUGGESTION: "Never throws" doc overclaims on `downloadArchiveBody`**

The new doc comment (bin/self_manage.dart:224) states:

```dart
/// Never throws: every failure is an [ArchiveDownloadOutcome].
```

but the implementation only guards `Exception`s:

```dart
} on TimeoutException catch (error) { … }
on Exception { … }           // stream errors + headers-phase failures
```

A non-`Exception` `Error` thrown by the transport or the stream (e.g. a `StateError` from a misbehaving client wrapper) would propagate out of `downloadArchiveBody` despite this contract. `applyUpdate` is safe (it has a catch-all `catch (_)` returning `downloadFailed`), but the `fa update` path — `runSelfUpdate` → `_binaryUpdate`/`fallbackZipUpdate` — has no catch-all, so such an error would surface as an unhandled crash with a stack trace instead of the clean `fa: download failed (network): …` message. (Old code had the same `on Exception` posture, so this is not a regression — the claim in the doc is what's new.)

Either tighten the wording ("never throws for `Exception` failures…") or catch `Object` in `downloadArchiveBody` and map it to `ArchiveDownloadOutcome.transport`. Optional polish, does not block merge.

**Key Issues**:
- 🚨 **Red CI gate**: `dart analyze --fatal-infos --fatal-warnings` exits 1 on `unnecessary_brace_in_string_interps` at `test/cli/self_manage_test.dart:1845:51` (reproduced locally — exactly this 1 issue; the size-budget `##[error]` lines in the log are expected fixtures of `scripts/test_size_manifest.py`, which passes).
- 💡 `downloadArchiveBody`'s "Never throws" doc overclaims — only `on Exception` is caught; a non-`Exception` `Error` still escapes on the `fa update` path (no catch-all there, unlike `applyUpdate`).

**Notes (no action required)**: worst-case body wall clock is now ~4 × 15 min (per-attempt backstop × 1 + 3 resumes) instead of the old 2-min total — documented per-attempt in the PR, and progress lines keep a slow update visible. Resumed bytes still pass the SHA256SUMS signature check, and a stall/reset never reaches provenance (AC4 verified by tests).
